canonicalization: docs/DESIGN.md section 4d, steps 1-4. Step 5 (body extraction) is a format concern and is not exercised by these fixtures.
contract: Every file in a group must produce that group's expected_digest, and no two groups may share one. Digests are regenerated deliberately, never as part of a code change.

groups.name: simple
groups.description: Two plain lines. Every file here differs only in line endings or in trailing whitespace, so all of them must produce one digest. This is the group that proves a mixed Windows/Unix team gets the same checksum for identical content.

files.note: CRLF and LF mixed in one file
no terminator on the last line
three blank lines at end of file
BOM, CRLF, trailing whitespace and a trailing blank line at once

groups.name: empty
groups.description: An empty result canonicalizes to the EMPTY STRING, not to a single newline (README, D-1). Its digest is the well-known sha256 of zero bytes, which makes this group a self-check on the implementation.

groups.name: interior-blank-lines
groups.description: Blank lines INSIDE the text are content and are preserved. This group must not share a digest with 'simple' -- if it does, the implementation is collapsing blank lines everywhere instead of only at the end.

files.note: one blank line between the two lines
the interior blank line carries spaces; it stays a blank line

groups.name: leading-blank-lines
groups.description: Leading blank lines are preserved; only TRAILING ones are stripped. This asymmetry is the reason both format contracts start a body at its first non-blank line.

files.note: one blank line at the start
leading blank line with spaces kept; trailing blank line stripped

groups.name: indentation
groups.description: Leading whitespace on a line is content; trailing whitespace is not. Gherkin is indented, so getting this backwards would change the digest of every .feature body.

files.note: spaces and a tab as indentation

groups.name: non-ascii
groups.description: Multi-byte UTF-8 must survive canonicalization byte for byte. Serbian Latin and Cyrillic, plus an emoji, so a byte-oriented trailing-whitespace strip that splits a code point shows up here.

files.note: BOM, CRLF, trailing whitespace, trailing blank line

groups.name: feature-body
groups.description: A realistic .feature body -- the actual thing a Confirmed-checksum is computed over (section 4). Proves the equivalence on real content, not only on toy input.

files.note: CRLF and no terminator on the last line
